title: Medical physiology: cells, nerves and muscle
audience: a medical student in the preclinical years
purpose: Apply homeostasis, body fluid compartments, membrane transport and potentials, action potentials, synaptic and neuromuscular transmission, skeletal, smooth and cardiac muscle, the autonomic nervous system, hormones and receptors, thermoregulation and exercise.

weeks.6: Synaptic transmission and the neuromuscular junction

blocks.deliverable: Compute fluid shifts after giving saline, water or dextrose.
Compute Nernst potentials and explain hyperkalemia's effect on excitability.
Explain how local anesthetics and myasthenia gravis affect conduction.
Week 7 midterm; compare excitation–contraction coupling in the three muscle types.
Predict organ responses to sympathetic and parasympathetic stimulation.
Explain cardiovascular and respiratory responses to exercise.
Submit the project; take an unseen 150 minute final in week 14.

project: Physiology problem set: compute osmolarity, Nernst and Goldman potentials and conduction effects for three clinical scenarios, with full reasoning.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
